content.text: {"cases":[{"id":"C1","instrument_review":"EFPA 9.3 (test-retest/temporal stability) reinterpreted as repeated-run stability. Only one run is reported and repetition is unstated, so reliability/precision would be rated 0 (insufficient information), not inadequate. Missing evidence is not proof of poor quality.","probes":[{"id":"repeat_test","label":"Not established","quote":"The report does not say whether runs were repeated.","reason":"No information on whether repeated runs were done."},{"id":"stable","label":"Not established","quote":"The tested system scored 70% in one reported run.","reason":"A single run cannot show stability; nothing else is supplied."}]},{"id":"C2","instrument_review":"EFPA 9.3 reinterpreted as run-to-run stability. The developers state that only one run was made, so no repeat reliability evidence exists (rating 0, no information). Stability is untested, not shown to be poor.","probes":[{"id":"repeat_test","label":"Contradicted","quote":"they ran the evaluation exactly once and did not repeat it","reason":"Explicitly no repeated runs."},{"id":"stable","label":"Not established","quote":"ran the evaluation exactly once","reason":"One run provides no evidence of stability, so it is unsupported rather than refuted."}]},{"id":"C3","instrument_review":"EFPA 9.3/9.7 reinterpreted: ten identical-condition repeats with a pre-defined stability criterion. Range 69-71% (2 points) meets the stated threshold, supporting adequate-or-better precision for this use. Only this benchmark and use are covered.","probes":[{"id":"repeat_test","label":"Supported","quote":"repeated the evaluation ten times with the same system, inputs, instructions, resources, and settings","reason":"Repeated runs under same conditions were done."},{"id":"stable","label":"Supported","quote":"Scores ranged from 69% to 71%.","reason":"A 2-point range meets the defined threshold of at most two points."}]},{"id":"C4","instrument_review":"EFPA 9.3/9.7 reinterpreted: ten identical-condition repeats were run, but a 20-90% range greatly exceeds the stated 2-point criterion. Precision would be rated inadequate (1) for this use.","probes":[{"id":"repeat_test","label":"Supported","quote":"repeated the evaluation ten times with the same system, inputs, instructions, resources, and settings","reason":"Repeats were conducted."},{"id":"stable","label":"Contradicted","quote":"Scores ranged from 20% to 90%.","reason":"A 70-point range far exceeds the two-point stability definition."}]},{"id":"C5","instrument_review":"EFPA 9.3 reinterpreted. The installation instructions concern materials/supply (section 6.3.8 software support) and add no reliability evidence. Repetition remains unstated, so the rating is 0 (no information).","probes":[{"id":"repeat_test","label":"Not established","quote":"The report does not say whether runs were repeated.","reason":"Installation instructions add no evaluation information."},{"id":"stable","label":"Not established","quote":"They report no additional evaluation results.","reason":"No stability evidence exists."}]},{"id":"C6","instrument_review":"EFPA 10.3 (relations to other variables) and the intended-use principle that validity concerns specific interpretations. The use is a narrow comparison on the evaluated puzzles, which the results support. Generalisation to general intelligence has no supporting evidence (10.3.1 not rated for it).","probes":[{"id":"narrow","label":"Supported","quote":"System A solves 80 puzzles and system B solves 60","reason":"Direct result matching the narrow intended use."},{"id":"broad","label":"Not established","quote":"Only grid puzzles were tested; no findings about other tasks are supplied.","reason":"No evidence beyond grid puzzles; unsupported, not refuted."}]},{"id":"C7","instrument_review":"EFPA 10 validity: the intended interpretation (general intelligence across domains) lacks content, structure, or criterion evidence. Validity for that use would be rated inadequate/insufficient, though the grid-puzzle comparison itself is reported.","probes":[{"id":"narrow","label":"Supported","quote":"System A solves 80 puzzles and system B solves 60","reason":"The grid-puzzle result is reported directly."},{"id":"broad","label":"Not established","quote":"no findings about other tasks are supplied","reason":"The stated use is broad but only grid evidence is given."}]},{"id":"C8","instrument_review":"EFPA 10.3.2 criterion evidence plus 10.3.1.6 (quasi)experimental designs, with reinterpretation for a workplace outcome. Test scores alone are not criterion evidence; the preregistered randomised trial with blinded checking supports correctness for the stated use (n=120, one workshop). Time/safety are not measured, so generalisation is limited.","probes":[{"id":"before","label":"Not established","quote":"Initially, only test scores were available.","reason":"No real-world outcome evidence existed at that stage."},{"id":"after","label":"Supported","quote":"With A, 90% of decisions were correct; with B, 70%.","reason":"Randomised, blinded trial with interval 12 to 28 points excluding zero."},{"id":"safety","label":"Not established","quote":"Time and safety outcomes were not measured.","reason":"Safety was not measured, so it cannot be established."}]},{"id":"P1A","instrument_review":"EFPA 9.3 reinterpreted as repeat-run stability. A single headline score and no execution history give rating 0, not inadequate.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Not established","quote":"gives no execution history","reason":"Unknown whether repeats were done."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Not established","quote":"one headline score of 75%","reason":"One score cannot show instability."}]},{"id":"P1B","instrument_review":"EFPA 9.3 reinterpreted. Only one evaluation exists, so stability is untested (rating 0), not shown to be unstable.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Contradicted","quote":"no repeat evaluations were conducted","reason":"Explicitly no repeats."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Not established","quote":"this was the only evaluation performed","reason":"Without repeats, instability is not demonstrated."}]},{"id":"P2A","instrument_review":"EFPA 9.3/9.7. Six repeats under identical conditions with a pre-defined threshold. Scores 73-75 give a range of 2, within the 3-point rule, so stability is supported.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"with identical inputs, settings and resources on six occasions","reason":"Stated directly."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Contradicted","quote":"maximum score range of three percentage points","reason":"The range is 75-73=2, within 3, so the rule is met."}]},{"id":"P2B","instrument_review":"EFPA 9.3/9.7. Six identical-condition repeats, but scores 51-82 (range 31) far exceed the 3-point rule, so precision is inadequate for this use.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"with identical inputs, settings and resources on six occasions","reason":"Stated directly."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Supported","quote":"The recorded scores are 51, 66, 79, 55, 82 and 62 percent.","reason":"A 31-point range exceeds the 3-point maximum."}]},{"id":"P3A","instrument_review":"EFPA 6.2 documentation and 9.3/6.1.7. Material describes topics and scoring only. No repeat-run or answer-error evidence, so those aspects are rated 0 (not possible to rate).","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Not established","quote":"It gives no execution history","reason":"No evidence of repeated evaluations."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Not established","quote":"no findings about mistakes in the provided answers","reason":"No findings either way."}]},{"id":"P3B","instrument_review":"EFPA 6.3.8 (software and technical support). The appendix covers installation only and adds no reliability or answer-quality evidence, so ratings remain 0 for those aspects.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Not established","quote":"It reports no further evaluation results or examination of answers.","reason":"Installation material adds no repeat evidence."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Not established","quote":"no further evaluation results or examination of answers","reason":"No examination of answers reported."}]},{"id":"P4A","instrument_review":"EFPA 6.1.3.2/6.1.3.3 item content development and review. Two independent editors examined all questions and answers, a good review process. No agreement count and no error findings are reported, so correctness of the final answers is not established (cf. 8.2.1.5 on agreement).","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"Two editors independently examined every question and supplied answer before release.","reason":"Both questions and answers were examined."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Not established","quote":"The report does not state whether mistakes were found or how many remained.","reason":"Review does not prove correctness."}]},{"id":"P4B","instrument_review":"EFPA 6.1.3 and 6.1.7. Independent examination occurred, but twelve answers are reported wrong in the released version, so item quality/key accuracy is inadequate (rating 1).","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"Two editors independently examined every question and supplied answer before release.","reason":"Examination of both occurred."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Contradicted","quote":"identifies twelve supplied answers as wrong in the released version","reason":"Explicit errors exist."}]},{"id":"P5A","instrument_review":"EFPA 9.6/9.7 and 6.3.2 (scoring checks). Deterministic scoring gives consistency but not accuracy. No validation against independent marks, so scoring accuracy is unrated (0).","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Contradicted","quote":"No comparison of those marks with independently established correct marks is reported.","reason":"Report says no such comparison is reported."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Not established","quote":"identical text always receives the same mark","reason":"Consistency is not correctness, and no accuracy evidence exists."}]},{"id":"P5B","instrument_review":"EFPA 6.3.2 and 9.6 reinterpreted. A 20-response check found 2 discrepancies, unresolved, with a small chosen sample. Scoring accuracy is questionable and rated inadequate to adequate at best.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"tested the software against independently established correct marks for 20 chosen responses","reason":"Stated directly."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Contradicted","quote":"Two marks differed and the discrepancies remain unresolved.","reason":"Discrepancies conflict with claim of correctness for all responses."}]},{"id":"P6A","instrument_review":"EFPA 10 intended-use validity. A narrow stated use (which system solved more of these 48 problems) is directly answered by the reported counts. Generalisation is not claimed.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"identifying which system solved more of these 48 grid problems in this evaluation","reason":"Counts 36 vs 24 suffice for this narrow use."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Supported","quote":"A solves 36 and B solves 24.","reason":"Direct result."}]},{"id":"P6B","instrument_review":"EFPA 10 intended-use validity. The stated use (general intelligence across subjects and real-world settings) is far broader than the evidence, giving inadequate validity for that use. The narrow result still stands.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Contradicted","quote":"No results from other tasks or settings are supplied.","reason":"The findings are insufficient for a broad claim as the passage itself indicates."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Supported","quote":"A solves 36 and B solves 24.","reason":"Direct result on the evaluated problems."}]},{"id":"P7A","instrument_review":"EFPA 3.2 scores and 6.1.3.1 test design justification. The all-or-nothing rule matches the stated requirement, so scoring is aligned with design.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"count only completely correct output grids","reason":"Rule matches requirement."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Contradicted","quote":"partial correctness is deliberately outside this comparison","reason":"Zero for partial grids is consistent with the requirement."}]},{"id":"P7B","instrument_review":"EFPA 6.1.3.1 and 6.3.2. The scoring rule gives no partial credit, contradicting the stated requirement of cell-level credit. Design is misaligned with the stated aim (inadequate).","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Contradicted","quote":"credit for every correctly completed cell, including partially correct output grids","reason":"The rule gives zero for partial grids."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Supported","quote":"A partially correct grid receives zero.","reason":"That conflicts with the cell-credit requirement."}]},{"id":"P8A","instrument_review":"EFPA 9.4 (equivalence/alternate forms) reinterpreted. Each evaluation changes the instruction, so this studies sensitivity to wording, not identical-condition repeat reliability.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Contradicted","quote":"No evaluation repeats an identical instruction.","reason":"Instructions differ, so conditions are not identical."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Supported","quote":"each evaluation uses a differently worded instruction","reason":"Score changes are reported across differently worded instructions."}]},{"id":"P8B","instrument_review":"EFPA 9.3 reinterpreted. Everything including instruction is held identical across evaluations, so this is repeat-run stability evidence. Instruction effects were not studied.","probes":[{"id":"claim1","label":"Supported","quote":"The software, resources, problem order, settings and instruction are identical on every evaluation.","reason":"Identical conditions."},{"id":"claim2","label":"Contradicted","quote":"No different instruction or presentation is studied.","reason":"Instruction effects were not studied."}]}],"closing_note":"Instructions were mostly clear. Ambiguities: EFPA-TRM is designed for human psychological tests, so sections such as norms, fairness and reports were not applicable or reinterpreted, and I used it only for explanatory framing. The 'Not established' vs 'Contradicted' boundary was applied by treating explicit conflict as Contradicted and absence of information as Not established. In C8 'before', the passage says only scores were available at first, treated as not establishing the claim."}
